name: Baha'i Faith
idea: Baha'i teaching treats service to humanity as a form of worship and speaks of tests and trials as part of spiritual growth, with deeds counting more than words. Abdu'l-Baha also urges kindness to strangers specifically. Baha'is understand these within belief in progressive revelation and in the oneness of humanity, so they sit near the guide's idea without being identical to it.

passages.text: if he seems to be lonely try to help him, give him of your willing service; if he be sad console him, if poor succour him, if oppressed rescue him, if in misery comfort him.
passages.ref: Abdul Baha, talk on the duty of kindness towards strangers and foreigners, Talks in Paris, 1911 to 1912
passages.translation: Talks by Abdul Baha Given in Paris, 3rd edition, London: G. Bell and Sons, 1916 (notes taken and translated from French)
passages.publisher: Internet Archive (scan of the original edition)

passages.text: Tests are benefits from God, for which we should thank Him. Grief and sorrow do not come to us by chance, they are sent to us by the Divine Mercy for our own perfecting.
passages.ref: Abdul Baha, Talks in Paris, p. 45
passages.translation: Talks by Abdul Baha Given in Paris, 3rd edition, London: G. Bell and Sons, 1916
passages.publisher: Internet Archive (scan of the original edition)

passages.text: those who proclaim their longing to make great sacrifices can only prove their truth by their deeds.
passages.ref: Abdul Baha, Talks in Paris, p. 44
passages.translation: Talks by Abdul Baha Given in Paris, 3rd edition, London: G. Bell and Sons, 1916
passages.publisher: Internet Archive (scan of the original edition)

passages.text: This is worship: to serve mankind and to minister to the needs of the people. Service is prayer.
passages.ref: Abdul Baha, Talks in Paris, section on prayer
passages.translation: Talks by Abdul Baha Given in Paris, 3rd edition, London: G. Bell and Sons, 1916
passages.publisher: Internet Archive (scan of the original edition)

practices.how: Speak to someone new to your community as a friend, and ask whether you can help with anything, as Abdu'l-Baha urged.

practices.do: Treat a test as a chance
practices.how: When something goes wrong this week, pause and ask what quality it asks of you, such as patience or gratitude, before reacting.
Use your work or craft for someone else's benefit, since Abdu'l-Baha counts work done in a spirit of service as worship.

practices.do: Hold yourself accountable at day's end
practices.how: Each evening, review your deeds as the Baha'i writings advise, and note where words and actions did not match.
Ask a local Baha'i community or neighborhood group where help is needed, and show up for one session.

ask: How do Baha'is understand the purpose of tests and trials in a person's life?
What does it look like to serve humanity in a way nobody sees or thanks?
How do you hold yourself accountable for your deeds from day to day?
caveat: These passages are from an early English rendering of notes on Abdu'l-Baha's talks, not from the authorized translations Baha'is now use, and Baha'is give primary authority to the writings of Baha'u'llah. This guide does not claim the Baha'i Faith teaches that life is a test set by a higher intelligence in the website's sense.
